levers.name: terminal growth stored as real rates on the house UAE path
levers.why: the two stages carried typed nominals of 2.5% and 1.5% and this study committed no macro record, so nothing held them to the house path
levers.evidence: THIS LEVER MOVES NO NUMBER, and the reason is the finding: this company's tariff is regulated and NOT indexed, so nominal revenue growth IS volume growth and the typed rates reproduce exactly as +0.49% and -0.49% real on the house 2.0% inflation. What it buys is a reader who can see that stage two assumes the business shrinks in real terms for ever — which the study describes as 'about zero real tariff growth' without ever naming the rate

note: THREE LEVERS AND ONLY ONE OF THEM MOVES THE VALUE, WHICH IS NOT THE USUAL SHAPE. The re-strike is arithmetic on a new price; the growth storage moves NOTHING, because a regulated unindexed tariff makes a typed nominal rate a volume assumption and the real component reproduces exactly; and the terminal rebuild is worth +0.7%. THE LEVER THAT MATTERED MOST IS NOT IN THE VALUE COLUMN AT ALL: publishing the four branches in the shared two-sided form changed no number and made the study visible to the one gate that examines the ANSWER, which had been skipping a +17% disagreement with the market for as long as this study has existed. Also recorded: the capital-per-unit-of-real-growth derivation used on the other four names in this programme computes NEGATIVE here (-388), because over five years the plant is written down faster than capex replaces it, and passing it through would have paid this company for growing.
